feedback.fb.h1: Tell us what broke. We will show you what changed.
feedback.fb.lead: Rocktier apps have no analytics and no telemetry, so the only way we hear about a problem is when you tell us. This page explains where to write, what we put on the record, and how to check that a fix really shipped.
feedback.fb.reach1: Inside any Rocktier app: open the Help menu and choose Send feedback. It opens a draft email on your device.
feedback.fb.reach2: Or write to hello@rocktier.com, or use the contact page. A short description, the app version and what you expected to happen are enough.
feedback.fb.reach3: Please do not attach private documents. A screenshot with the sensitive parts removed is usually more useful than the file itself.
feedback.fb.publishTitle: What we publish, and what we do not
feedback.fb.publish1: We have no user reviews that we are allowed to publish yet, so this page has no star ratings, no selected praise and no quotes. We will not invent any.
feedback.fb.publish2: When someone lets us quote them, we will print the words unchanged, the unflattering ones too, next to the version that addressed them. Until then, the honest record is the changelog.
feedback.fb.logTitle: A fix log you can check
feedback.fb.logLead: These entries are copied from our public changelog, with real version numbers. None of them is presented as a response to a user email: they came from our own checks and from what we found while testing. Follow the link to read the full log.
feedback.fb.log1: 2026-11-03, Rocktier Markdown 1.0.20: the preview's synced indicator could stay dark even when both panes were in sync. Fixed.
feedback.fb.log2: 2026-10-24, Rocktier Markdown 1.0.17: Intel Mac builds added, so the app runs on older Macs as well as Apple Silicon.
feedback.fb.log3: 2026-10-25, Rocktier OCR 0.2.11: an earlier update had removed the interface and the app opened to a blank window. The interface was put back.
feedback.fb.log4: 2026-11-04, Rocktier Pic2WebP 1.9.20: in the default window the convert button could sit below the visible area. It now stays visible while only the settings scroll.
feedback.fb.after1: We try to reproduce it on the same platform. If we cannot, we will write back and ask for one more detail.
feedback.fb.after2: We fix the cause, not just the symptom, and add a check that would have caught it earlier.
feedback.fb.after3: The change goes into the public changelog with its version number, so you can verify the claim instead of taking our word for it.
feedback.fb.after4: We cannot promise every report lands in the next release. We can promise we will not quietly drop it, and that we will tell you if we decide not to do it.

journal.jr.f4.t: Searchable, and easy to back up
journal.jr.f4.b: Full-text search finds the day you half remember, and backup export produces an encrypted ZIP you can store anywhere you like.

open-md.openmd.lead: A .md file is just plain text, so any text editor can show you the raw characters. To see headings, tables, code blocks and images as a page, open it with a Markdown app. Here are the ways that work on both Windows and macOS.
open-md.openmd.whatBody: Markdown uses plain punctuation for structure: a # for a heading, dashes for a list, backticks for code. The file stays readable forever, because it is text. A Markdown app renders those marks into a formatted page and, if you want, lets you edit the text beside it.
open-md.openmd.mac1: Install the app once, then double-click any .md file in Finder. If another app is set as the default, right-click the file, choose Open With, and pick Rocktier Markdown.
open-md.openmd.mac2: You can also drag the file onto the app icon in the Dock, or onto an open window.
open-md.openmd.mac3: To make it stick, use Get Info, set Open With, then click Change All. macOS will remember it for that extension.
open-md.openmd.win1: Install the app once, then double-click the file in File Explorer. If it opens in Notepad, right-click, choose Open with, then Choose another app and pick Rocktier Markdown.
open-md.openmd.win2: Tick "Always use this app to open .md files" in that dialog to make it the default.
open-md.openmd.win3: Dragging the file onto an open window works too, and skips the default-app setting entirely.
open-md.openmd.extBody: Rocktier Markdown registers eight common Markdown extensions. They are all plain text, so even a file with an unusual extension can be opened from inside the app with File, then Open.
open-md.openmd.fixTitle: When it does not look right
open-md.openmd.fix1: You see the raw marks instead of a page: the file is open in a plain text editor. Change the default app as described above.
open-md.openmd.fix2: Images are missing: Markdown stores image paths, not the images. Keep the pictures next to the .md file, or use paths that still resolve from where the file lives.
open-md.openmd.fix3: Chinese text is garbled: the file was saved in a legacy encoding. Re-save it as UTF-8, which is what Markdown apps expect.

privacy.privacy.title: Your files never leave your device.
privacy.privacy.sub: One privacy policy for the whole Rocktier family. Every app works on your files locally, and no app connects to the internet unless you ask it to. No accounts, no uploads, no tracking.
privacy.privacy.scopeP: This policy applies to every Rocktier app and to rocktier.com. The current family: Rocktier PDF, Rocktier Pic2WebP, Rocktier Markdown, Rocktier OCR, Rocktier CAD Viewer, Rocktier Write, Rocktier Journal and Rocktier Compressor. Each new app that joins is covered by this same policy.
privacy.privacy.collectP1: Rocktier apps are built so they need no personal information to work. We ask for no name, no email, no phone number, no location, and no account. There is nothing to sign up for, and we run no usage analytics.
privacy.privacy.collectP2: The files you compress, convert, edit, merge, or sign are processed on your device and never leave it. We have no servers that receive them and no way to see them.
privacy.privacy.collectP3: Our apps contain no telemetry, no advertising SDKs, and no third-party analytics of any kind. If a version ever offers crash reporting, it is off by default: a report is sent only after you approve that specific report, and declining it costs you nothing.
privacy.privacy.collectP4: A Rocktier app can make at most two kinds of requests, both described in full below: a license activation, and an update check that also re-checks your licence status. Both happen only when you ask for them: by entering a license code, or by clicking "Check for updates". Neither is needed to use the app, and it works fully offline without them. Some versions distributed through an app store ship without both entry points, because the store handles purchase and updates. A build that offers neither of them makes no network requests at all.
privacy.privacy.listP: Across the family, these are the only three requests a direct-download build can make. They map to the two kinds described above: activation, and update checking (which may contact both our server and GitHub). Every one of them needs you to act first; none happens at startup or in the background, and none carries file contents, file names or paths.
privacy.privacy.list1: when you enter a license code. Sends the code, a device fingerprint used for the activation limit, and the OS name.
privacy.privacy.list2: when you click "Check for updates" while a receipt exists. Sends only the transaction id already in that receipt.
privacy.privacy.list3: when you click "Check for updates". A public API call with no body, no query parameters and no custom fields; the repository name is part of the URL.
privacy.privacy.listNote: Some app-store builds omit the menu entries that trigger these requests. What is left in a given build is visible in its Help menu, and the two kinds of request described above are the only ones any of them can make.
privacy.privacy.updateP1: No Rocktier app checks for updates on its own. The app does not connect to the internet when it starts, while you work, or in the background. When you click "Check for updates", the app requests one small file that lists the latest version: and that is the only thing it asks for.
privacy.privacy.updateP2: That request is a plain GET to GitHub's public releases API. The app sends no body, no query parameters and no custom fields: the repository name is part of the URL, and the only header the app sets is Accept. Standard request information: such as your IP address and the User-Agent supplied by your system, which may identify your operating system and CPU: is handled by GitHub under its own privacy policy, and we do not receive it. The request never carries your license code, your device identifier, or anything about your files. If a newer version exists, the app tells you and links to the official release page. We never download or install anything without asking, and we do not track which version you run.
privacy.privacy.updateP3: Activating a license is a separate request to our own server. Its reply contains only a signed receipt, the product code and your device count: it does not return a version number, and the app never asks for one. On the latest releases, clicking "Check for updates" also re-checks your licence status with our server once: the request carries only the transaction id already in your receipt, and a refunded licence is deactivated locally. A build that ships without both entry points sends nothing to us.
privacy.privacy.licenseP1: Activation is the only action that sends an identifier, and it happens only when you choose to activate a license or manage your devices. The app sends your license code, a device identifier, and the name of your operating system, so that we can count activations against the device limit and let you release a machine you no longer use.
privacy.privacy.licenseP2: We store the license code, the device identifier, and the activation date. We store nothing else, and your documents are never involved.
privacy.privacy.processP: All work happens locally on your device using its native capabilities, with no internet needed. Closing an app or deleting it removes its data from your device; nothing is kept anywhere else.
privacy.privacy.shareP1: We do not sell, rent, trade, or share your data with anyone, for any reason.
privacy.privacy.shareP2: When you download an app from a store (Microsoft Store, Apple App Store, or similar), the store operator handles standard transaction and device information under its own privacy policy. That handling is governed by the store operator, not by us, and we receive no personal data from it.
privacy.privacy.secureP: Your data lives only on your device, protected by your operating system's own measures: app sandboxing, file permissions, and encryption at rest. There is no Rocktier cloud, no Rocktier database, and no data center that can be breached.
privacy.privacy.kidsP: Rocktier apps are not directed at children under 13 and do not knowingly collect any data from anyone, including children. In practice, there is nothing of yours, or of a child's, for us to hold.
privacy.privacy.rightsP: Under the GDPR (EU/UK), CCPA/CPRA (California), and China's PIPL, you have the right to access, correct, delete, and export your personal data. Because Rocktier collects no personal data, these rights are met by design. For any question, contact us and we will respond within 30 days.

vs-online-tools.vs.safetyLead: Uploading is harmless for a public meme, and unacceptable for the documents most people actually need to compress or convert:
vs-online-tools.vs.safety1Body: Client agreements and signed documents are confidential by definition; a compression tool has no business keeping a copy.
vs-online-tools.vs.safety2Body: In many jurisdictions (HIPAA, GDPR) passing them through a third-party server can create compliance exposure you never agreed to.
vs-online-tools.vs.safety3Body: "We delete files after one hour" is a policy, not a guarantee, and it is theirs to change.
vs-online-tools.vs.safety4Body: Uploading gigabytes of personal photos to convert them to WebP wastes time and bandwidth you did not need to spend.
vs-online-tools.vs.safetyVerdict: for anything private, offline wins: nothing is uploaded, so nothing can be retained, leaked, or read.
vs-online-tools.vs-online-tools.h2.1: What do online PDF tools really cost?
vs-online-tools.vs.costLead: Subscription pricing is how these tools make money: and the free tier exists to show you its own limits:
vs-online-tools.vs.cost2Body: iLovePDF's free plan caps file sizes (merge 100 MB, compress 200 MB) and daily usage (compress: 2 files per day); Smallpdf limits free downloads per day across its tools.
vs-online-tools.vs.cost3Body: metered and retried whenever the quota resets: the work stops until tomorrow.
vs-online-tools.vs.costVerdict: Rocktier apps cost $4.99-$14.99 once (Rocktier PDF is $9.99: about ten weeks of iLovePDF Premium), and never ask for another payment, an account, or a connection.
vs-online-tools.vs-online-tools.h2.2: Is local processing slower than a data center?
vs-online-tools.vs.speedBody: A data center computes fast, but the bottleneck is not the computing: it is the round-trip. A 50 MB scan takes seconds to upload on a good connection and minutes on a bad one, then the result travels back. Processing the same file locally takes about a second and starts the moment you drop it.
vs-online-tools.vs.speedVerdict: for typical files, local wins on speed: the upload never happens, and neither does the queue.
vs-online-tools.vs.faq1q: Are desktop tools harder to install than a website?
vs-online-tools.vs.faq1a: A Rocktier download is a single installer under 15 MB. You install it once and it stays out of your way: no account, no browser tab, no waiting for a server queue.
vs-online-tools.vs.faq2q: Is local processing slower than a data center?
vs-online-tools.vs.faq2a: For typical files, no. Uploading and downloading usually takes longer than the processing itself. Modern machines compress a PDF or convert a photo in about a second.
vs-online-tools.vs.faq3q: Why pay once instead of using a free web tool?
vs-online-tools.vs.faq3a: Free online tools monetize with ads, quotas, and your attention (and sometimes your data). Rocktier costs from $4.99 once: no renewals, no caps, no ads.
vs-online-tools.vs.faq4q: Do the tools still get updates?
vs-online-tools.vs.faq4a: Yes. Updates are included in the one-time purchase. You are never asked to pay again.
vs-online-tools.vs.faq5q: Do web tools upload my files to their servers?
vs-online-tools.vs.faq5a: Yes, that is how browser tools work by design: the file is uploaded, processed on their servers, and sent back. Rocktier apps never upload; the file is processed on your machine.

keys.privacy.collectP1: Rocktier 应用的设计目标：不靠任何个人信息也能干活。我们不要姓名、邮箱、电话、位置，也没有账号体系。没什么要注册的，我们也不做使用分析。
keys.privacy.collectP2: 你压缩、转换、编辑、合并、签署的文件，都在你设备上处理，一步不离开。我们没有接收这些文件的服务器，想看也看不了。
keys.privacy.collectP3: 应用里没有遥测，没有广告 SDK，没有任何第三方分析。将来哪个版本要是加了崩溃上报，默认也是关的：你同意发那一份，它才发；不同意，你什么也不损失。
keys.privacy.collectP4: Rocktier 应用最多发两类请求，下面细说：激活许可证，和检查更新（已授权的用户点「检查更新」时，会顺带复核一次许可状态）。都得你主动开口才算：输激活码，或者点「检查更新」。不联网照样完整使用。有些从应用商店装的版本连这两个入口都没做进去，购买和更新交给商店；只有两个入口都没做进去的构建，才是一次网络请求都不发的。
keys.privacy.listP: 整个家族里，直发版能发出的请求只有下面三条。它们对应上面那两类：激活，和检查更新（可能同时问我们自己的服务器和 GitHub）。每一条都要你先动手；启动时没有，后台也没有；都不带文件内容、文件名和路径。
keys.privacy.list1: 输入激活码时发出。带激活码、用于计算激活次数的设备指纹，以及操作系统名称。
keys.privacy.list2: 已持有回执时，点「检查更新」发出。只带回执里已经有的那个交易号。
keys.privacy.list3: 点「检查更新」时发出。一次公开接口的读取：没有请求正文，没有网址参数，没有自定义字段；仓库名只出现在网址里。
keys.privacy.listNote: 有些从应用商店装的版本没有做进这些菜单项。某份构建还留着哪些，看它自己的帮助菜单就知道；而它们能发出的请求，不会超出上面那两类。
keys.privacy.updateP1: 没有哪款 Rocktier 应用会自己检查更新：启动时不联网，你干活时不联网，后台也不联网。你点了「检查更新」，它才去要一个小文件——里面只有最新版本号，它也只问这一个。
keys.privacy.updateP2: 这个请求就是向 GitHub 公开接口发一次普通的读取：不带请求正文，不带网址参数，也不带任何自定义字段；仓库名只出现在网址里，应用自己设的请求头只有一项格式声明。网络地址、系统自带的浏览器标识（可能含操作系统和 CPU 信息）这类标准请求信息，由 GitHub 按它自己的隐私政策处理，我们收不到。它不带激活码、设备标识，更不带你文件的任何信息。有新版本，应用会告诉你，并给出官方发布页链接。不跟你打招呼，我们不会下载或安装任何东西，也不记你用的哪个版本。
keys.privacy.updateP3: 激活许可证是发给我们自己服务器的另一个请求，回复里只有一张签名回执、产品码和设备数，不返回版本号，应用也不会去问。最新版本里，点「检查更新」还会顺带向我们的服务器核对一次许可状态：只带交易号，就你买完收到的回执里那个；已退款的许可会在本地停用。两个入口都没做进去的构建，对我们这边一个请求都不发。
keys.privacy.licenseP1: 激活是唯一会发出标识信息的动作，而且只发生在你主动激活许可证或管理设备的时候。应用会发激活码、设备标识和操作系统名称，好让我们核对激活数有没有超上限，也方便你解绑不再用的机器。
keys.privacy.licenseP2: 我们只存激活码、设备标识和激活日期，别的不存。你的文档从来不掺和这些数据。
keys.privacy.processP: 所有处理都在你自己的设备上完成，用它自己的能力，不需要联网。卸掉或删掉某个应用，它在你设备上的数据一起走；别的地方，什么都不会留。
keys.privacy.shareP1: 你的数据，我们不出售、不出租、不交易，也不跟任何人分享——什么理由都不行。
keys.privacy.shareP2: 从应用商店（Microsoft Store、Apple App Store 或类似渠道）下载时，商店会按它自己的隐私政策处理标准的交易和设备信息。那是商店的事，不归我们管，我们也收不到你的任何个人信息。
keys.privacy.secureP: 你的数据只存在于你的设备上，由操作系统的自带措施保护：应用沙盒、文件权限和静态加密。没有 Rocktier 云、没有 Rocktier 数据库，也没有可以被攻破的数据中心。
keys.privacy.kidsP: Rocktier 应用不面向 13 岁以下的儿童，也不会故意收集任何人的数据，孩子的也不行。说实在的：我们手里什么都没有——你的没有，孩子的也没有。
keys.privacy.rightsP: 在 GDPR（欧盟/英国）、CCPA/CPRA（加州）和中国《个人信息保护法》下，你有权访问、更正、删除、导出你的个人数据。我们不收集个人数据，这些权利天然就满足了。有疑问？找我们，30 天内回复。
keys.privacy.webP: 本站不用 cookie，不做分析，不投广告。你的主题偏好存在浏览器的 localStorage 里，只待在你自己的设备上。网站由 Vercel 托管，它会按自己的隐私政策存标准服务器日志（比如 IP 地址和访问时间）。
keys.privacy.changesP: 政策要改，我们会更新上方的「最后更新」日期；改动大，会在本页说明。家族再大，政策还是这一份。
keys.privacy.controllerP: Rocktier 由武汉汉阳罗克网络科技工作室运营。本政策涉及的这点有限的个人信息处理，由该工作室作为数据控制者负责。

keys.vs-online-tools.h2: 离线处理比上传更安全吗？
keys.vs.safetyLead: 上传一张公开的表情包无所谓，但大多数人真正要压缩或转换的文件，不该这么处理：
keys.vs.safety1Body: 客户协议和已签文件按定义就是机密；一个压缩工具没有理由留副本。
keys.vs.safety2Body: 在很多司法辖区（HIPAA、GDPR），让这些文件经过第三方服务器，可能给你带来从未同意过的合规风险。
keys.vs.safety3Label: 受保密协议约束的客户工作。
keys.vs.safety3Body: 「一小时后自动删除」是政策，不是保证，而且改不改由它们说了算。
keys.vs.safety4Body: 把几个 GB 的个人照片上传去转 WebP，浪费的是你本不必花的时间和带宽。
keys.vs.safetyVerdict: 只要涉及隐私，离线就赢——什么都没上传，也就没东西可保留、泄露或被读取。

keys.vs.faq2q: 本地处理比数据中心慢吗？
keys.vs.speedBody: 数据中心算得快，但瓶颈不在算力，而在往返。一个 50 MB 的扫描件，网好时上传也要几秒，网差时要几分钟，处理完还得传回来。同一个文件在本地处理大约一秒，拖进去就开始。
keys.vs.speedVerdict: 对常见文件，本地在速度上赢——没有上传，也没有排队。

keys.vs.faq3q: 为什么要一次买断，而不是用免费网页工具？

keys.vs.faq5q: 网页工具会把我的文件上传到服务器吗？
keys.vs.faq5a: 会——浏览器工具就是这么工作的：文件被上传，在它们的服务器上处理，再送回来。Rocktier 应用从不上传，文件在你的机器上处理。
